about.title: Tracy Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Tracy sits where I-205 funnels commuter traffic between the Central Valley and the Bay Area, and the daily rhythm of that corridor shapes how collisions happen here. In 2025, the city recorded 221 injury collisions, with 304 people injured and 2 traffic deaths. Public-record counts run highest along I-205, Grant Line Road, Corral Hollow Road, and 11th Street, and reported crashes tend to cluster on Fridays between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m. Behind each number is someone dealing with a totaled car, a sore neck that turned into something worse, and an insurance adjuster who wants a statement before the dust settles. LawProactive exists to take one task off that list. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Tracy residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims in San Joaquin County on a contingency basis. You describe what happened; we make the introduction. There is no charge to you for the connection, and no attorney fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Tracy Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines that sneak up on you
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident claim, but if a city vehicle or public road condition is involved, that window can shrink to six months. The attorney we connect you with can sort out which deadline applies to your Tracy crash.

items.title: Partial blame does not end your claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly responsible; your share of fault reduces the amount rather than erasing it. That matters when the other driver's insurer tries to pin more on you than the facts support.

items.title: Nothing out of pocket to get started
items.desc: Our connection is free, and network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no attorney fee unless money is recovered. California also places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in ordinary car accident cases, so your full losses stay on the table.

items.question: I was hit on I-205 near Tracy but I live in another county. Does that matter?
items.answer: Not for getting help. Where the crash happened is what usually determines which court would hear a lawsuit, and an attorney familiar with San Joaquin County can handle that even if you live elsewhere. What matters more right now is preserving the CHP report, photos, and any dashcam or witness details from the scene.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company called and wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other side's insurer a recorded statement, and it is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift fault onto you under California's comparative fault rule. Politely take their contact information and let a lawyer handle the conversation.

items.question: How much does it cost to use LawProactive after a Tracy car accident?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm; we simply connect you with an independent personal injury attorney. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they are paid a percentage only if your case results in a recovery, and you owe no attorney fee if it does not.
